text:
Lane Hutson scored both Montreal goals in Carolina on Thursday, including the overtime winner, and the Canadiens went home on a two-game winning streak at 14-5-4. Eric Engels of Sportsnet called it a gutsy win, and it fits a team that keeps finding points it has to scrap for.

The scrapping matters because the underlying play is roughly even. Montreal gets 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at all strengths, and our points from the play come to 23.8 against the 32 they have. The difference is mostly in net: the Canadiens have allowed 13.7 fewer goals than expected. Jacob Fowler, now leading Calder talk per The Hockey News, has saved 4.4 goals above expected over his last five starts.

The lineup is thin up front. Ivan Demidov has been out since fracturing his ankle in the preseason, and Chris Kreider is out six to eight weeks with a lower-body injury, per NHL.com. The Phillip Danault, Alexandre Texier and Zachary Bolduc line has kept chances down best of the regular lines, with 61% of them. Juraj Slafkovsky has 5 points in his last 10 against 7.7 our numbers expected, a cold spell rather than a collapse. The Noah Dobson and Hutson pair drives play at 57%.

Montreal is 71% to make the playoffs by our odds. What we'd watch is the penalty kill and the discipline: the Canadiens take 4.7 penalties a game, and that's a lot to ask of a rookie goalie.
headline: The Canadiens are winning ahead of their chances
